display.title: What to Think When We Say the Shema: Hashem Is Our Strength and Our Life
display.summary_short: Mitzvah Time on the Shema: what Shema, Elokeinu and Echad mean, and what to think about while saying them.
display.summary_long: A Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, part of a series on reciting the Shema morning and evening. Uncle Yossi reviews the meaning of each word. Shema is a command to listen, and our Sages teach that it also means to understand. Elokeinu means 'our God', and it also means our strength and our life: every bit of strength we have, and life itself, comes from Hashem. Echad means one, and its three letters hint that Hashem, the Master of the world, rules over the seven heavens and the earth and over all four directions. So when we cover our eyes and say the Shema, we think that Hashem is our God, our strength and our life, and the one Creator of everything. The lesson ends with a review of everything learned so far about the Shema: the words, when to say them, what to do and what to think.
display.lesson: When you say the Shema, think that Hashem is our God, our strength and our life, and the only Creator of everything.
